content.text:
I couldn't see the source of `jwt.strategy.ts` or `auth.service.ts`, so these candidates are inferred from the graph structure and the symptom. I haven't confirmed them against the code.

Login and refresh both succeed, so token signing and the refresh strategy are probably fine. Only requests that use the access-token guard fail with 401. That points to the access-token verification in `JwtStrategy`.

candidates.explanation: Most likely cause (inferred, not confirmed against the code). The access-token strategy's passport-jwt options (secretOrKey, jwtFromRequest, ignoreExpiration) probably don't match how access tokens are signed. For example, it may read `auth.refreshSecret` instead of `auth.secret`, or use the wrong token extractor. Every freshly issued access token then fails verification and gets a 401, while login and refresh still work because the refresh strategy and signing are separate.

If the payload check is wrong, for example it tests a field the access token doesn't carry such as `payload.sessionId` instead of `payload.id`, or throws UnauthorizedException on valid payloads, every valid access token is rejected.

If the access token is signed with the wrong secret (such as the refresh secret), has an already-elapsed expiry, or omits the `id` claim, it will fail JwtStrategy verification even though login and refresh themselves succeed.

fix.description: Make the JwtStrategy options match how access tokens are signed. Use `configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret')` as `secretOrKey`, use `ExtractJwt.fromAuthHeaderAsBearerToken()`, and set `ignoreExpiration: false`. In `validate`, only reject the payload when `!payload.id`, then return the payload. Also check that `getTokensData` signs the access token with `auth.secret` and `auth.expires`.
